title: To Descendants
subtitle: What we leave behind, and what you will remember.

trails.title: Damp Paperslip
trails.description: The writer must have been in a rush, leaving it to share space with crates and the cold wind.

content.text: Lost Export Plan Found at Port

Raw Coal:

Commonly used as a fuel for combustion. Suitable for heating and power generation. High priority for direct export (but can cause resource waste and air pollution).

Coal Gasification:

Can be converted into clean fuel gas for synthesis (related technology and facilities are expensive – consider collaborative production methods).

Coal Ash:

Produced from boiler combustion. Can be recycled for use in road construction. No need for export.

Coking Coal:

Important material for iron smelting (perhaps the ironworks could be rebuilt?).

In addition: It is reported that there is technology to produce refined coal after it is washed, and there is a high demand for refined coal in the south. Should be prioritized.

What is the source of this report? Who could have predicted that we would uncover a coal mine, or that we had been to the south?

—Comrade Evgeni listed more than a dozen common uses and export directions for energy in his letter, and we found one that we could use.

trails.title: Production Factory

content.speaker: Illia
content.text: Kiril, it's time to get back to work! Please remind Bogina to come down from the forklift and stop playing Sudoku. We have to deliver the wood for reinforcing the mine roof by tonight.

content.speaker: Illia
content.text: Oh, Knut! What brings you here? It's not yet time for the shift change.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: I'm not here for the shift change. I'm actually just dropping off some parts and a toolbox we found. Take a look, it's fully stocked.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: I couldn't help but notice Comrade Kiril standing off to the side, spinning in circles. It almost made me dizzy when I first arrived.

content.speaker: Illia
content.text: He's been acting like this since the lunch break started, while Bogina is engrossed in her usual game. I wonder what's going on with Kiril ...

content.speaker: Kiril
content.text: Illia, you haven't had the chance to read Comrade Evgeni's letter, so you don't know.

content.speaker: Kiril
content.text: Looking at the stains on my hands from the coal dust, I can't help but think of his letter again. I find myself pacing back and forth, imagining how my comrades will lay me to rest when my time comes. It would be a great honor, but also ...

content.speaker: Kiril
content.text: I can't help but feel that Comrade Evgeni deserved a different fate than this.

content.speaker: Kiril
content.text: He did not deserve to end his journey in this place.

content.speaker: Illia
content.text: Kiril ...
Comrade Knut was the first to find the letter. Later we all took turns touching it, like passing around a flag, remember?
You shouldn't talk like that to Illia, and you shouldn't think like that about comrade Evgeni.

content.speaker: Kiril
content.text: But you said the same thing earlier, Bogina.

content.speaker: Bogina
content.text: Yes, I said that. But I also said—

content.speaker: Bogina
content.text: "Comrade Evgeni ended his journey here, but we must go on."

content.speaker: Bogina
content.text: With only one square left to fill in the Sudoku, it's clear that this is the only way to go.

content.speaker: Bogina
content.text: "Keep moving forward, to a better tomorrow."

content.speaker: Illia
content.text: This is not the end of our journey, Comrade Kiril.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: Right ... I may not be good with words, but I wholeheartedly agree with comrade Bogina.

content.speaker: Knut
content.text: This must have been Comrade Evgeni's true wish.

trails.title: Snow
trails.description: Tiny salt crystals scattered across the ground, faithful companions that can fix any problem.

content.text: Snow and Other Possibilities

To the town, she is a familiar figure. But to herself, everything is so drastically different.

She's used to walking in the snow. The poplar fluff floating through Moscow's streets reminds her of Rayashki; it's like snow, but it doesn't make her cheeks turn red or her hands and feet cold; it doesn't melt on the skin, nor can it hide anything. Canned goods, even sausages and fresh meat, are available in stores, and one doesn't have to count the days just to exchange for everyday items ... The first time she made soup in her new home, it felt surreal. Another vivid memory was when she got off the train, holding her child's hand in fear. Outside the small town, in Moscow, there were so many people, all seemingly full of hope. 

But she boarded the train back to Rayashki anyway.

Rayashki had changed, too. There were faces in the town she didn't recognize, and the statue in the center of the square had changed. The school was still the same, and the children played games in the small playground. The townspeople's greetings were a bit awkward; no one mentioned her hasty departure as if it was not important, as if anyone could leave at any time and also return whenever they wanted.

Snow fell on her hair and collar, turning her fingers and nose red—this was real snow.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: It's good to see you again, Comrade Ulyana. I heard that you have returned.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Did you get a chance to go to see the children? They've been going on about you for so long.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: It's been a while since I've been back to this town. How are the little ones doing? With you watching over them, I'm sure they're doing fine. You've always been such a caring teacher.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: But there is only so much that one person can do. It would be great to have another comrade to lend a hand.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: So, will you stay this time, Comrade Ulyana?

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: Right. I wanted to talk to you about that ...

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: We can take our time to talk, no need to rush. By the way, did little Vasya come with you?

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Now that our supplies are fully stocked, we can take the children to the square tomorrow for some sketching ...

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: It's just me this time, Comrade Vila.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: Back in Moscow, my thoughts kept returning to Rayashki. Those who have chosen to stay here are incredibly determined and tenacious. They are genuinely sincere and kind, but they are very stubborn in their beliefs. Does that make any sense?

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: In Moscow, you don't have to worry about cold temperatures or lack of resources. If children need pencils, they can simply go to the nearest store and buy them.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: That sounds like a dream come true! We're doing everything we can to make Rayashki just that.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: It was really beautiful, but when I sat next to Vasya's bed, when he was fighting his asthma, with the poplar fuzz in the air ... And then children's gravestones and coffins, so tiny and fragile, almost like toys ... I could hardly believe they were real.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: I clung to the hope that life would get better in Moscow. I believed that if I just endured and persevered a little longer, things would turn around.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: But that was not the way it turned out.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: My sincerest condolences, Comrade Ulyana.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: It's alright, I brought it up myself. When I was in the house in Moscow, I couldn't stop crying. But eventually I realized that I had to pull myself together and do something.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: Is it still possible for me to reunite with everyone? Looking back, I regret leaving in such a selfish manner.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: The future is unknown and unpredictable. All we can do is take one step at a time on the path that lies ahead of us.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: You will always have the ability to move forward on this path, with all of us.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Don't all crowd around us at once, kids. Give us some space so that Miss Ulyana, your teacher, can greet you, okay?

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: Hooray! We're super happy you're teaching again, Miss Ulyana! Tee-hee!

content.speaker: Pasono
content.text: Miss Ulyana! There are soo many new things in town that I can't wait to show you!

content.speaker: Pyotr
content.text: Me too! I know this town like the back of my hand, and I've got a sneaky shortcut to the mine to show you!

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: Of course, my little bears, my patient little comrades.

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: Here. I received this as a gift from the square, and I want to share it with you. Vila always tells us to share with others.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: What a beautiful sunflower. Thank you, Avgust. Say, you seem much happier now.

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: I notice that my mom and everyone else around me are smiling, so I can't help but smile too.

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: You're smiling too, Ulyana.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: Haha, yes. I, I really missed you all.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Aw, don't rub your eyes with your hands, kids. Here's some handkerchiefs for you ...

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: It took you kids a long time to come up with that welcome. Don't forget to actually say it to Miss Ulyana.

content.speaker: The Kids
content.text: —Welcome home, Miss Ulyana!

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: The welcome and the celebration, all arranged on the same day ... Rayashki is slowly gaining momentum again, but there's still so much to do. I hope you don't mind.

content.speaker: Ulyana
content.text: No, not at all. How can I be of help? Just let me know.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Would you mind taking care of the children for a while? I have to go check on the port soon, and some friends from the Foundation are coming over for their regular lectures. Please make sure they are held to the same standards as our agreement. And finally ...

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Welcome home, Comrade Ulyana!

trails.title: Laborer's Canteen
trails.description: The bigger the occasion, the more preparation is needed. Our comrades deserve this well-orchestrated celebration.

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: I've finished folding it, Comrade Pyotr. It's time to make our paper planes fly. Can you move a little? Just a bit!

content.speaker: Pyotr
content.text: Alright! Let's see whose plane can fly the farthest!

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: Three, two, one!

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: The swallow dives into the snow pile. Pyotr wins.

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: He hasn't flown his yet, Comrade Avgust, maybe ...

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: Hey, Pasono, are you not going to play with us?

content.speaker: Pasono
content.text: ... I've been thinking about what Miss Vila said.

content.speaker: Pyotr
content.text: Are you scared? Don't you want to go out and see? After all, our parents agreed, and adults always know better than we do.

content.speaker: Pasono
content.text: I'm not scared! But... Miss Vila said she will not go with us, neither will Miss Ulyana.

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: Vila has a lot to do. After the slow turtles left, many new friends came to town. Vila wants to talk to them.

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: I don't think we need to worry so much. The teachers have allowed these friends of the Foundation to attend our classes, play with us, and take notes ...

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: They don't seem like bad people. If they were bad, Miss Vila would shoo them away.

content.speaker: Pyotr
content.text: That's right, Pasono! Even Avgust isn't as anxious as you are!

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: I'm not nervous, I just want to learn how to transform things. Like turning a sunflower into a towering soldier or a bear with round ears ...

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: We could turn snowmen into us to keep Vila company. Mom always said that when we miss her, we should build a snowman.

content.speaker: Avgust
content.text: —And Vila will definitely miss us when we're gone.

content.speaker: Pyotr
content.text: Yes, we should leave a gift for Miss Vila! Let's go make some snowmen!

content.speaker: Nina
content.text: Alright!

content.speaker: Pasono
content.text: Yes, let's find the prettiest twigs to decorate them with!

content.speaker: Pyotr
content.text: Let's go, everyone. Split up to find materials and come back as quickly as we can!

trails.title: Twig Collecting Initiative
trails.description: Even when building snowmen, these kids have a keen eye for good materials.

trails.title: Abandoned Mines
trails.description: Pay attention to the vibrant colors around the mine, and don't lose sight of the child busy building a snowman.

trails.title: Children's Creation
trails.description: Shaped by different little hands, sharing the same innocent hopes.

content.text: Circle Dance

Snowmen of various sizes were arranged in a circle on the playground, and the children lovingly linked their twig arms together so that the snow friends were holding hands. Each child focused on decorating their little creation, staying close together, and when one arm brushed another's shoulder, there was a cheerful laugh.

The little girl on the far left lowered her head, her braids curled up like haystacks in the sun. She carefully placed sunflower petals on her snowman's head. Nearby, two boys were trying to make their snowman's chubby body wider and sturdier so it would last longer and Ms. Vila could greet them more often.

The little boy's snowman was a bear. It was only through his explanation that the head and paws of the arctic fox could be seen on its back. Foxes don't usually have long ears like rabbits, but he gave it those in order to hear his mother's footsteps, Vila's footsteps, and his friends' footsteps. Finally, he carefully placed the mined ore on the fox's chest, just as he wore the beautiful stone his father had left him.

"Okay, my frosty comrades! You can all stay here and do the circle dance with Ms. Vila. Remember, no running around or making a ruckus; just listen to her instructions ..."

trails.title: The Workers
trails.description: Those who made Rayashki stand tall on the snowy plains, and those who never expected their names to be remembered.

content.text: Caring Crowd

Among the long tables sits a group of people.

The one in the middle maintains her usual politeness and friendly smile. If you weren't looking at how her hands are resting uncertainly on the table, you'd miss the emotion beyond the politeness. Yes, this young scholar is stunned that the theory she has been focusing on is back in the spotlight. After being relegated to the pile of old papers in most places outside, it has found a place in Rayashki.

As for the people around her, most are still wearing their work clothes, with coal dust clinging to their collars and pant legs. They are aware of this and keep their distance from the scholar until she reaches out to them. This group of makeshift teachers and students shake hands, determined to spend time understanding a fading discipline. Those most dedicated to the work are also the most serious pragmatists. The study of ley lines has played such an important role in the rebuilding of the town! When the scholar first entered the research institute, this is what she had hoped for. Is the study of ley lines omnipotent? No. But it may eventually bring about change.

Perhaps it will be the moment the coal mine was discovered, or perhaps it is this moment.

trails.title: Unexpected Scenario
trails.description: An impromptu lecture on the study of ley lines. The architect never imagined that this place would be used for such passionate discussions.

trails.title: Residential Area
trails.description: The best way to solve local problems is to consult with the locals. The most direct approach is to go door to door.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: Wow. I'm getting a little nervous.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: There are a lot of new faces here, quite unexpected. Well, hopefully a midday vodka will calm my nerves.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: May I have your attention, please? Comrades and visitors, welcome to today's lecture on the study of ley lines.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: I am Windsong, your speaker for today.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: Now, I will present some practical examples on how the Study of Ley Lines can be applied to the mineral development in Rayashki ...

content.speaker: Laplace Researcher
content.text: This is undoubtedly beneficial to our research. Who cares about other people's opinions? Personally, I find Ley Lines very useful and relevant.

content.speaker: Laplace Researcher
content.text: We definitely need to try this out and tell Ms. Lucy about it. I have no doubt she would be intrigued by this type of presentation ...

content.speaker: Laplace Researcher
content.text: I'll take thorough notes. I'll be prepared in case there's a Q&A session later.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Hello, there!

content.speaker: Laplace Researcher
content.text: Uh? Oh. Hello, ma'am.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: If you need a seat closer to the front, I can take you to the visitor's seats over there.

content.speaker: Laplace Researcher
content.text: No thank you, I'm not a typical guest like them. I'm here as a researcher.

content.speaker: Laplace Researcher
content.text: Is there somewhere I can hear more clearly? Does Ms. Windsong have any other business to attend to? I have a list of questions written down, such as methods for identifying lines ...

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: There will be a Q&A session after the presentation. Follow me and we'll see if there's a better location for you that's closer and more spacious.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: Phew, I really need a drink. This is as tiring as any physical labor.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: I hope the Q&A session won't be met with dead silence. Just in case, I have prepared a couple of basic talking points ...

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: Comrade Windsong, here.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: Perfect. This glass of water couldn't have come at a better time.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: The lecture went smoothly, and I still have time to make it to today's performance. As I promised to Avgust and the others, I have a little trick with ley lines that will surely amaze them.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: The Study of Ley Lines is much more than just a little trick, Comrade Windsong. We all know this to be true.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: The woman from Laplace has technical inquiries for you. You might want to finish your drink, I have a feeling she has quite a few questions lined up.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: She can ask all she wants about the subject. The truth is, I'll be researching Ley Lines for a long time to come.

content.speaker: Windsong
content.text: What are your thoughts on this lecture? I welcome constructive criticism, so feel free to share your honest opinions, Comrade Vila.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: It brought back memories of a "line" I had seen before, although it's not exactly the same as your ley lines.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: One morning I was floating on the surface of the water, admiring the distant shore. The horizon line seemed impossibly far away, with a soft glow radiating from it.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: At that moment, I decided to go and see for myself. And so I arrived at Rayashki, my footprints leaving marks in the snow as I watched it transform into what it is today.

content.speaker: Vila
content.text: ... It's remarkable how our dreams are gradually becoming a reality.

items.text: The river of time has moved swiftly in the passing months.
Rayashki is bustling with the sounds of a busy and hopeful community.
Crowds of people, lively and spirited, weave to-and-fro.
Swimming Pool, Rayashki
A disheveled figure hurries into the scene.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Thank goodness! I was hoping you'd be here!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh, erm, is this a bad time?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Heh heh, no, it's alright. Have a seat.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm not a pure Rusalka. As you can see, I must get in touch with water every once in a while to replenish my power from the ocean.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Ahem. Hello, Comrade Vila.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It's been a while, Comrade Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They say you're working hard in the mine, and the study of ley lines is getting popular among the workers.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: They have helped a lot. My research on the environment wouldn't have gone nearly so smoothly without them.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's given a second life to my studies, and it is growing so well. It has even gained some recognition beyond Rayashki.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I, I'm truly happy that I came here.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I never thought the Comrade Windsong would be so bashful over her accomplishments. I thought you were more stubborn and confident than that.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm only teasing, comrade. It's a matter of fact that you are not as fearless as you pretend to be, isn't it?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's why we must all stick together to make up for each other's weaknesses and make Rayashki proud! Sorry, speeches have become an occupational habit.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Fine, you got me. But it's not a big deal. Just as you are not quite the gentle and demure school teacher that you appear to be, are you, comrade?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We're even!
Windsong clears her throat and hands the letter to Vila.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Actually, I've come to say goodbye.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Laplace has invited me to give a lecture for their European branch. They want me to give a lecture on how I combined environmental analysis with the arcanum based on what we've done here in Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Sounds like a very promising new beginning for your studies.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: How are things going in the town?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We are getting more visitors now. It seems people are eager to see something different.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'm sure they will.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We've also begun cooperating with many governments and agencies near us, including the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They hope to carry out some short-term training on the arcanum for the children.
Another letter is passed on.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: What's this?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Open it. It's from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Mr. Name Day invites me to visit the Foundation and discuss further cooperation. The children are also waiting for me there.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It seems they mentioned you all the time during their training.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Did we miss the ley line exam?"

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "The Foundation has all sorts of incredible things."

items.speaker: "Avgust"
items.text: Like biting coins, noisy coal balls, a glass pen with rainbows inside. So much fun!

items.speaker: "Pasono"
items.text: I've mastered a lot of incantations!

items.speaker: "Nina"
items.text: I miss the town and everyone.

items.speaker: "Avgust"
items.text: Yeah. We miss Comrade Alenka, Comrade Blinchik, and Comrade Piroshki!

items.speaker: "Pyotr"
items.text: They say we will be able to go home in a few months!

items.speaker: "Pyotr"
items.text: I must master the most powerful arcane skills by then, so I can use them to protect the town!

items.speaker: "Avgust"
items.text: We'll transform into sea swallows!

items.speaker: "Avgust"
items.text: Then we'll be able to fly and fly to far, far away!

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster I
items.text: The Kaslinska University Hospital received a rare case today.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster I
items.text: The patient's veins irreversibly transformed into electric wires. As of 18:00, all arterial, venous, and capillary tissues throughout the patient's body have undergone necrosis.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster I
items.text: The director said they would invite more professionals to the consultation to decide on further research directions.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster I
items.text: Global Variety News has claimed the case may become one of the greatest unsolved mysteries of the era.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster I
items.text: They started a new column to analyze possible compatibilities between the patient's new wired veins and different appliances.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster I
items.text: Please stay tuned for more details.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster II
items.text: The Flying Carpet Travel Agency is starting a tour around Northern Europe ...

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster II
items.text: ... where you will be able to see the breathtaking aurora borealis, pet fluffy Qiqirns, and even enjoy a flying carpet race.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster II
items.text: The destination of our tour is Rayashki.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster II
items.text: A mysterious town, the warmest place in the Arctic Circle, sitting atop many rich veins of coal.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster II
items.text: When you get there, we suggest that you abide by the town's wishes and work to earn what you need instead of buying it. Though this is not an obligation, of course.

items.speaker: Radio Broadcaster II
items.text: But why not have a try when you are given the opportunity to experience a new and better lifestyle? Trust me, you won't be disappointed.
Heh heh.
Where should I start, dear readers?
Rayashki is like a sparkling gem embedded into the permafrost. And above flies an eye-catching banner. Perhaps it will draw even more attention in the future.
Through the past decades, the citizens there have been trying to achieve something different for themselves.
A great cause which may take the work of generations to achieve.
But now they are no longer a nameless town in the far north, nor is their dream a passing fad bound to be forgotten.
I sincerely hope all of us will be able to witness its history and its future.
That's why I knew I must write down this story. In the hopes that their dream will remain in your heart forever.
